3	#
4	# Consumed by:

6	#   - .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl
7	#   - .chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl
8	# via `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` at render time. `include`
9	# (not `includeTemplate`) is used because this file is plain bash, not a
10	# chezmoi template — no `{{ … }}` tokens need re-rendering.
11	#
12	# WHY inlined instead of sourced: each run_*.sh.tmpl is rendered by chezmoi
13	# to a temp path and executed there; at runtime it has no reliable route back
14	# to the source tree, so `source` would be fragile. Inlining keeps one
15	# source-of-truth here while placing the code wherever it is needed.
16	# Bonus: `scripts/**` is listed in .chezmoiignore.tmpl so this file is never
17	# deployed to $HOME — its only existence at runtime is the inlined copy.
18	#
19	# Lifetime:
20	#   - State dir `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/` (or $TMPDIR fallback),
21	#     mode 0700, contains:
22	#       sudo.pass           0600  raw password (one line, terminating \n)
23	#       ansible-become.yml  0600  `ansible_become_password: "…"` for `-e @`
24	#       keepalive.pid       0600  detached watchdog PID
25	#       chezmoi.pid         0600  ancestor chezmoi PID the watchdog watches
26	#   - Watchdog is detached via `setsid` so a run-script EXIT does not reap it.
27	#     It watches the chezmoi ancestor PID and `rm -rf`s the state dir when
28	#     chezmoi exits. That is the effective end-of-flow cleanup — per-script
29	#     EXIT traps would wipe state before the NEXT run-script could reuse it.
30	#   - INT/TERM/HUP in any consuming script triggers `sudo_session_abort`,
31	#     which kills the watchdog and wipes state immediately.
32	#
33	# Public API:
34	#   sudo_session_init [label]   Idempotent. If state valid, re-export vars and
35	#                               return. Else probe passwordless sudo; if not
36	#                               passwordless, prompt once on /dev/tty, validate,
37	#                               write files, spawn watchdog. Returns non-zero if
38	#                               no TTY available and not passwordless.
39	#                               Non-interactive override: when env var
40	#                               CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE points to a 0600 file
41	#                               containing the password, the file is adopted
42	#                               instead of prompting (used by remote orchestrators
43	#                               like scripts/fleet_apply.py — see docs/this_repo/
44	#                               fleet-apply.md).
45	#   sudo_session_skip_reason    Print a one-word label the caller uses to pick
46	#                               a branch: "cached" | "passwordless" |
47	#                               "non-interactive" | "" (empty = not probed yet).
48	#                               Safe to call before OR after sudo_session_init.
49	#   sudo_session_abort          Signal handler target — kill watchdog, wipe state.
50	#   sudo_run <cmd...>           `sudo -S` wrapper that pipes the cached password
51	#                               from the state file; no password ever in argv.
52	#                               Falls back to plain `sudo` when passwordless.
53	#   sudo_session_warm_cache     Best-effort: refresh the CURRENT TTY's sudo
54	#                               timestamp using the cached password (for callers
55	#                               like `brew bundle` whose cask pkg installers
56	#                               invoke `sudo /usr/sbin/installer` internally).
57	#
58	# Exports on success:
59	#   CHEZMOI_SUDO_STATE_DIR  CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASS_FILE
60	#   CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE  CHEZMOI_SUDO_KEEPALIVE_PID

65	        printf '%s/chezmoi-sudo-%s\n' "$base" "$(id -u)"
66	    else

71	# Walk the parent chain looking for a `chezmoi` process; prints its PID, or
72	# empty on miss. Cross-platform: /proc on Linux, ps on macOS.
73	_sudo_find_chezmoi_ancestor() {
74	    local pid="${PPID:-0}"
75	    local comm=""
76	    local hops=0
77	    while [[ "$pid" -gt 1 && "$hops" -lt 20 ]]; do
78	        if [[ -r "/proc/$pid/comm" ]]; then
79	            comm="$(cat "/proc/$pid/comm" 2>/dev/null || printf '')"
80	        else
81	            comm="$(ps -o comm= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==1{n=split($0,a,"/"); print a[n]}')"
82	        fi
83	        if [[ "$comm" == "chezmoi" ]]; then
84	            printf '%s\n' "$pid"
85	            return 0
86	        fi
87	        if [[ -r "/proc/$pid/status" ]]; then
88	            pid="$(awk '/^PPid:/ {print $2; exit}' "/proc/$pid/status" 2>/dev/null)"
89	        else
90	            pid="$(ps -o ppid= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')"
91	        fi
92	        [[ -n "$pid" && "$pid" != "0" ]] || break
93	        hops=$((hops + 1))
94	    done
95	    printf ''

120	    # positional params, so single-quoting is intentional (no expansion here).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-24 20:01:32Z)**_

**Root cause: `setsid` doesn't exist on macOS.**

In `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh:122`, the watchdog is spawned with:

```bash
setsid bash -c '…' _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
```

On this Mac (`which setsid` → not found), the backgrounded invocation dies instantly with "command not found". But `$!` still captures the short-lived shell PID, which gets written to `keepalive.pid` and survives as a pointer to a ghost process.

Then on the next script, `_sudo_state_valid` (`sudo_shared.sh:98`) fails at line 105:

```bash
kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1   # watchdog PID is long dead → returns 1
```

`sudo_session_init` treats the state as stale, wipes the dir at line 236, and re-prompts. That's why you see three `[bootstrap]` / `[ansible]` / `[brew]` prompts instead of one.

Evidence from your machine:
- `which setsid` → not found
- `keepalive.pid` contains `33387`, `kill -0 33387` → DEAD, `ps -p 33387` → no row
- State dir exists with valid `sudo.pass` / `ansible-become.yml`, but the missing watchdog kills the idempotency check

Linux machines ship `setsid` via util-linux, so this bug is macOS-only — which matches why no one has noticed on Ubuntu hosts.

**Fix:** fall back to `nohup` (or a pure `bash` + `trap '' HUP` + `disown`) when `setsid` isn't available. Sketch:

```bash
_sudo_spawn_watchdog() {
    local state_dir="$1" watch_pid="$2"
    local body='
        trap "" HUP
        while kill -0 "$2" 2>/dev/null; do
            sudo -S -v -p "" <"$1/sudo.pass" 2>/dev/null || true
            sleep 50
        done
        rm -rf "$1"
    '
    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        setsid bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    else
        nohup bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    fi
    local pid=$!
    disown 2>/dev/null || true
    printf '%s\n' "$pid"
}
```

`nohup` exists on macOS (`/usr/bin/nohup`) and also handles SIGHUP-on-terminal-hangup, so combined with `disown` the detachment is close enough to `setsid` for this use case.

Want me to apply the fix and add a `pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md` entry? It meets the graduation bar (silent failure, non-obvious, would recur on every new macOS box).

有，但要分兩層看：

## 1. `setsid(2)` system call：macOS 有

macOS / Darwin 有 `setsid()` 這個 libc/system call。Apple 的 man page 寫得跟 Linux 很像：`setsid()` 會建立新的 session，呼叫者成為新的 session leader / process group leader，且沒有 controlling terminal。([Apple Developer][1])

所以 C / Python 這種程式裡可以用：

```python
import os

os.setsid()
```

或更推薦在 `subprocess` 用：

```python
import subprocess

subprocess.Popen(
    ["your-command"],
    start_new_session=True,
)
```

## 2. `setsid(1)` command：macOS 通常沒有內建

Linux 上常見的：

```bash
setsid my_command
```

這個是 `setsid(1)` 命令，通常來自 util-linux。macOS 預設一般沒有 `/usr/bin/setsid`；但可以透過 Homebrew 安裝 `util-linux`，Homebrew 目前有 `util-linux` formula，不過它是 **keg-only**，所以裝完後不一定直接出現在 `$PATH`。([Homebrew Formulae][2])

可以試：

```bash
which setsid
man 2 setsid
```

大概率是：

```text
setsid not found
```

但：

```bash
man 2 setsid
```

可能有。

## macOS 上實務上怎麼做？

如果你只是想「關掉 terminal 後繼續跑」：

```bash
nohup your_command > out.log 2>&1 &
disown
```

如果你是在 Python 裡啟動 subprocess，最乾淨是：

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess


def run_detached(command: list[str]) -> subprocess.Popen[bytes]:
    return subprocess.Popen(
        command,
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        start_new_session=True,
    )
```

如果你是真的要做 macOS 的長期 background job，官方路線其實不是手寫 daemon + `setsid`，而是用 **launchd / launchctl**。Apple 文件也說 macOS 用 `launchd` 管理 daemons 和 agents，可以用它跑 shell scripts。([Apple Support][3])

一句話：

> macOS 有 `setsid()` 這個底層能力，但通常沒有 Linux 那個 `setsid` CLI。臨時用 `nohup ... & disown`；Python 用 `start_new_session=True`；正式服務用 `launchd`。

[1]: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/System/Conceptual/ManPages_iPhoneOS/man2/setsid.2.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Mac OS X Manual Page For setsid(2)"
[2]: https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/util-linux?utm_source=chatgpt.com "util-linux"
[3]: https://support.apple.com/guide/terminal/script-management-with-launchd-apdc6c1077b-5d5d-4d35-9c19-60f2397b2369/mac?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Script management with launchd in Terminal on Mac"
```

114	_sudo_spawn_watchdog() {
115	    local state_dir="$1"
116	    local watch_pid="$2"
117	    # setsid detaches from the controlling TTY + session so the watchdog is
118	    # not reaped when the invoking run-script exits normally.
119	    # SC2016: body is passed to the child `bash -c` where $1/$2 are its own
120	    # positional params, so single-quoting is intentional (no expansion here).
121	    # shellcheck disable=SC2016
122	    setsid bash -c '
123	        STATE_DIR="$1"
124	        WATCH_PID="$2"
125	        # WHY: the real "keep-alive" is the sudo.pass + `sudo -S` pattern —
126	        # we still refresh the timestamp opportunistically so short-lived
127	        # downstream callers may benefit. Failures (tty_tickets mismatch,
128	        # stale password) are swallowed; they are not cleanup triggers.
129	        while kill -0 "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
130	            sudo -S -v -p "" <"$STATE_DIR/sudo.pass" 2>/dev/null || true
131	            sleep 50
132	        done
133	        rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
134	    ' _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
135	    local pid=$!
136	    disown 2>/dev/null || true
137	    printf '%s\n' "$pid"
138	}
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Pitfalls
2	
3	Past traps we've stepped on. Symptoms-first knowledge base — the goal is that
4	when a problem recurs (on a new machine, after an upgrade, with a new tool
5	combo), grepping the symptom here lands you on the root cause and workaround
6	in seconds, instead of re-debugging from scratch.
7	
8	This folder is `chezmoi`-ignored (see `.chezmoiignore.tmpl` → `pitfalls/**`); it
9	is repo metadata for maintainers, not user-facing config to deploy.
10	
11	## Pitfalls vs the rest
12	
13	This repo has four sibling surfaces with overlapping shapes; pick the right one:
14	
15	| Surface | Time direction | Question it answers | Access pattern |
16	|---|---|---|---|
17	| `docs/tools/<tool>.md` | Present | "How does this tool work / how do I configure it?" | Read top to bottom |
18	| `docs/this_repo/<topic>.md` | Present | "Why did we architect it this way?" | Read top to bottom |
19	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptoms** |
20	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "We thought about doing Y — what was the analysis?" | Index in `TODO.md` |
21	| `AGENTS.md` Hard invariants | Present | "What rules MUST agents follow?" | Read top to bottom |
22	
23	A pitfall **graduates** to a Hard invariant in `AGENTS.md` when the trap is
24	serious enough that you can't rely on memory or grep — typically when (a) it
25	recurs across machines, (b) it silently corrupts state, or (c) the workaround
26	is non-obvious and easy to undo by accident. When graduating, leave a
27	`pitfalls/<slug>.md` as historical record and link to it from the invariant.
28	
29	## When to add a pitfall doc
30	
31	Add a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` when you've spent more than ~15 minutes on something
32	where the answer wasn't googleable, AND any of:
33	
34	- The symptom is non-obvious from the root cause (`SSH_CONNECTION` cleared
35	  silently → hostname module disappears, no error)
36	- The fix is "do nothing different but in a specific order" (sentinel writes
37	  must come after `wait $pid` for fleet-apply, etc.)
38	- The same trap could be hit by a new agent / new machine / new contributor
39	- An upstream bug exists with no ETA — workaround needs to outlive memory
40	- A specific tool version is required (or forbidden) and the failure mode at
41	  the wrong version is silent / confusing (e.g. tmux 3.2a popup off-screen)
42	
43	## When NOT to add a pitfall doc
44	
45	- Trivially googleable error (the next person will solve in 30 seconds anyway)
46	- Already covered in `docs/tools/<tool>.md` as part of the tool's normal
47	  configuration — cross-link from this README's "Cross-referenced pitfalls"
48	  table below instead of duplicating
49	- Already a `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant — those have higher priority enforcement
50	  (cross-link only)
51	- One-off transient (network glitch, machine-specific config rot) — fix and
52	  move on
53	
54	## File template
55	
56	See [`assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`](#) in the
57	[`project-knowledge-harness` skill](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness),
58	or copy the structure of an existing entry below.
59	
60	Key sections (different from `backlog/` template — symptom-first, not
61	context-first):
62	
63	```markdown
64	# <Title describing the SYMPTOM, not the root cause>
65	
66	**Symptoms** (grep this section): <verbatim error messages, observable behaviour>
67	**First seen**: YYYY-MM
68	**Affects**: <tool/version/OS combo>
69	**Status**: workaround documented / fixed upstream in vX.Y / WONTFIX
70	
71	## Symptom
72	
73	Full error messages (verbatim, not paraphrased — preserves grep-ability).
74	Reproduction steps if applicable.
75	
76	## Root cause
77	
78	Why this happens. Reference source, docs, or upstream issue.
79	
80	## Workaround
81	
82	Immediate workaround (commands, config diff). Should be copy-pasteable.
83	
84	## Prevention
85	
86	How to avoid stepping on this again. If serious enough, link to the
87	corresponding `AGENTS.md` Hard invariant.
88	
89	## Related
90	
91	Links to `docs/`, sibling pitfalls, `TODO.md` entries (if a real fix is
92	queued), upstream issues/PRs.
93	```
94

```text
1	# `chezmoi apply` in noRoot mode fails with `sudo: a password is required` at an ansible task (missing `tags: [sudo]`)
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- On a host provisioned with `noRoot=true`, `chezmoi apply` runs the ansible
5	  phase, reports most tasks `ok`, then fails abruptly at ONE task with:
6	  ```
7	  [ERROR]: Task failed: Premature end of stream waiting for become success.
8	  >>> Standard Error
9	  sudo: a password is required
10	  Origin: /home/<user>/.ansible/roles/<role>/tasks/main.yml:<N>:3
11	  ```
12	- `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2` → whole `chezmoi apply`
13	  aborts, downstream `run_*` scripts never execute
14	- The same task runs cleanly on rooted dev boxes, so CI/testing doesn't catch it
15	- Exactly reproducible: `ssh HOST chezmoi apply` fails at the same task on every
16	  invocation until the ansible YAML is patched
17	
18	**First seen**: 2026-04 on `jingle-207` (Ubuntu 22.04, `ubuntu_server` profile,
19	`noRoot=true`), task `devtools : Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)`
20	at `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:2415`
21	**Affects**: any ansible task in this repo that has `become: true` but NO
22	`tags: [sudo]`, executed on a host where `noRoot=true` was chosen at
23	`chezmoi init`
24	**Status**: workaround = add the missing tag. Structural prevention = repo
25	convention (see [Prevention](#prevention)).
26	
27	## Symptom
28	
29	Full failing output from the noRoot host:
30	
31	```
32	[71] TASK · [devtools : Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)]
33	[ERROR]: Task failed: Premature end of stream waiting for become success.
34	>>> Standard Error
35	sudo: a password is required
36	Origin: /home/ldw/.ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:2415:3
37	
38	2413     PATH: "{{ ansible_facts['env']['HOME'] }}/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:{{ ansible_facts['env']['PATH'] }}"
39	2414
40	2415 - name: Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)
41	       ^ column 3
42	
43	✘ fatal: [localhost]: FAILED! (0.5s) =>
44	    changed: false
45	    msg: |-
46	        Task failed: Premature end of stream waiting for become success.
47	        >>> Standard Error
48	        sudo: a password is required
49	```
50	
51	```
52	localhost                  : ok=70   changed=4    unreachable=0    failed=1    skipped=199  rescued=0    ignored=0
53	chezmoi: 20_ansible_roles.sh: exit status 2
54	```
55	
56	The offending YAML at the time (missing the tag):
57	
58	```yaml
59	- name: Ensure xz is available for worktrunk extraction (Debian/Ubuntu)
60	  when:
61	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
62	    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
63	  ansible.builtin.apt:
64	    name: xz-utils
65	    state: present
66	  become: true
67	  failed_when: false      # ← `failed_when: false` doesn't help here
68	  # ← missing: tags: [sudo]
69	```
70	
71	## Root cause
72	
73	noRoot mode in this repo is NOT implemented as an ansible variable (e.g.
74	`no_root: true` with `when: not no_root`). It is implemented at the **shell
75	wrapper** layer, in `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:249` (approx):
76	
77	```bash
78	{{ if $noRoot -}}
79	info "noRoot mode enabled - installing user-level tools to ~/.local/bin"
80	...
81	BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"
82	{{- end }}
83	```
84	
85	Which becomes, at invocation time:
86	
87	```bash
88	ansible-playbook -i "$INVENTORY" "$PLAYBOOK" --tags "$TAGS" --skip-tags sudo …
89	```
90	
91	The mechanism is `ansible-playbook --skip-tags sudo` — so any task that wants
92	to be skipped on noRoot hosts MUST declare `tags: [sudo]`. A task with
93	`become: true` but without the tag will:
94	
95	1. Bypass the `--skip-tags sudo` filter (no matching tag to skip)
96	2. Hit the `become: true` escalation path
97	3. Ansible's become plugin (`sudo` by default) tries to acquire root
98	4. The sudoers config on noRoot hosts doesn't grant passwordless sudo to the
99	   user → `sudo` emits `a password is required` on stderr and exits non-zero
100	5. Ansible interprets this as "Premature end of stream waiting for become
101	   success" → task fails → play aborts
102	
103	Why `failed_when: false` doesn't save you: `failed_when: false` evaluates the
104	**module result**. The failure above happens in the **become handshake**,
105	before the module ever runs. Ansible treats become failures as fatal
106	regardless of `failed_when` / `ignore_errors`.
107	
108	Why tagging works: a `--skip-tags sudo` match is evaluated during task
109	scheduling, before become is attempted. The task is dropped from the play
110	entirely, the sudoers prompt never happens.
111	
112	## Workaround
113	
114	Add the tag to the offending task. Canonical pattern (from
115	`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3115`, which gets this right):
116	
117	```yaml
118	- name: Ensure xz-utils is available for jnv tarball extraction
119	  when:
120	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
121	    - jnv_recheck.rc != 0
122	  become: true
123	  tags: [sudo]             # ← required for noRoot hosts
124	  ansible.builtin.apt:
125	    name: xz-utils
126	    state: present
127	  failed_when: false
128	```
129	
130	Note the ordering: `become: true` / `tags: [sudo]` / module declaration is the
131	style used across this repo. Match it for consistency.
132	
133	If the skipped task means a downstream user-level install path also can't
134	succeed (e.g. the xz apt skip means a `.tar.xz` unarchive downstream will
135	fail), add a **probe + gate** so the downstream block doesn't waste bandwidth
136	and time:
137	
138	```yaml
139	- name: Probe for xz binary (worktrunk extraction dependency)
140	  when:
141	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
142	    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
143	  ansible.builtin.shell: command -v xz || true
144	  args: { executable: /bin/bash }
145	  register: worktrunk_xz_probe
146	  changed_when: false
147	
148	- name: Install worktrunk from GitHub releases (Debian/Ubuntu, user-level)
149	  when:
150	    - ansible_facts["os_family"] == "Debian"
151	    - worktrunk_check.rc != 0
152	    - target_architecture in ['x86_64', 'amd64', 'aarch64', 'arm64']
153	    - worktrunk_xz_probe.stdout | default('') | trim != ''   # ← skip when xz absent
154	  block:
155	    ...
156	```
157	
158	## Prevention
159	
160	**Repo convention**: any ansible task in `dot_ansible/roles/**` that uses
161	`become: true` MUST also declare `tags: [sudo]`. No exceptions — even for
162	tasks you're "sure" won't run on noRoot hosts, because the profile
163	combinations drift over time.
164	
165	**Manual audit** before merging a PR that adds or edits become-using tasks:
166	
167	```bash
168	# Find `become: true` lines that are NOT followed within ~5 lines by tags: [sudo]
169	# (crude — manually review the hits)
170	cd /home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi
171	rg -n -B 0 -A 5 '^\s*become:\s*true' dot_ansible/ | less
172	```
173	
174	Or more targeted, if ripgrep supports multiline (it does with `--multiline`):
175	
176	```bash
177	rg --multiline --multiline-dotall -U \
178	   'become:\s*true(?![^\n]*\n\s*tags:\s*\[sudo\]|[^\n]*\n[^\n]*\n\s*tags:\s*\[sudo\])' \
179	   dot_ansible/
180	```
181	
182	Expect false positives around handlers (`become:` in a handler doesn't need
183	`tags:` if the handler is only notified from tagged tasks) — eyeball the
184	matches, don't auto-fix.
185	
186	**Local test for noRoot mode** (before committing the ansible change):
187	
188	```bash
189	# Simulate noRoot by running ansible directly with --skip-tags sudo
190	cd /home/ldw/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible
191	ansible-playbook -i localhost, -c local setup.yml.tmpl \
192	  --tags devtools --skip-tags sudo --check
193	```
194	
195	The `--check` flag is crucial — in normal mode it would try to actually run
196	apt, which is what you're trying to prove is skipped.
197	
198	## Related
199	
200	- [CLAUDE.md § Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts](../CLAUDE.md) —
201	  describes the full sudo-helper flow that noRoot mode short-circuits
202	- [`pitfalls/npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md`](npm-postinstall-github-releases-hang.md)
203	  — sibling "this only breaks on one host profile" pitfall, different root
204	  cause (network vs sudoers)
205	- `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:3115` — reference pattern (jnv
206	  xz-utils task, gets it right)
207	- `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl:249` — where
208	  `BECOME_FLAGS="--skip-tags sudo"` is set for noRoot runs
209
```
</details></tool-use>

# Shared sudo session re-prompts once per run-script on macOS (`setsid` missing)

**Symptoms** (grep this section):
- On macOS, `chezmoi apply` (or `chezmoi update --init`) prompts three times
  in a row — once per run-script — despite the "entered once, reused for this
  chezmoi apply" wording:
  \```
  [bootstrap] sudo password for <user> (entered once, reused for this chezmoi apply):
  …
  [ansible]   sudo password for <user> (entered once, reused for this chezmoi apply):
  …
  [brew]      sudo password for <user> (entered once, reused for this chezmoi apply):
  \```
- `which setsid` on macOS: `setsid not found`
- `man 2 setsid` exists (libc system call), but `setsid(1)` does not ship in
  base macOS
- Between prompts, `$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/` exists with valid `sudo.pass`
  / `ansible-become.yml` / `keepalive.pid`, but the PID in `keepalive.pid` is
  dead: `kill -0 $(cat …/keepalive.pid)` returns non-zero, `ps -p <pid>`
  returns no row
- Linux hosts (Ubuntu, Debian) are unaffected — util-linux ships `setsid(1)`
- No `setsid: command not found` error is visible to the user because the
  failing command is backgrounded with `>/dev/null 2>&1 &`

**First seen**: 2026-04 on `Da-Weis-Mac-mini` (macOS 26.2 arm64, chezmoi 2.69.4)
**Affects**: any macOS host running `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` without
util-linux installed from Homebrew. Introduced when the shared-sudo helper
landed.
**Status**: fixed in `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` (`_sudo_spawn_watchdog`
falls back to `nohup` when `setsid` is unavailable).

## Symptom

The helper's contract is "prompt once at the start of `chezmoi apply`,
downstream run-scripts reuse the cached credential silently" (see
[CLAUDE.md → Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts](../CLAUDE.md)).
On macOS the prompt fires three separate times — once for `bootstrap`, once
for `ansible`, once for `brew` — with the state dir being wiped and rebuilt
between each.

The state on disk during the second prompt looks "valid":

\```
$ ls -la "$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)"
.rw-------@ 36 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  ansible-become.yml
.rw-------@  6 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  chezmoi.pid
.rw-------@  6 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  keepalive.pid
.rw-------@  9 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  sudo.pass

$ PID=$(cat "$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)/keepalive.pid")
$ kill -0 "$PID" 2>&1 || echo DEAD
DEAD
$ ps -p "$PID"
  PID TTY           TIME CMD       # empty — process long gone
\```

`sudo.pass` is correct; `ansible-become.yml` is correct; the watchdog is the
only broken piece.

## Root cause

`_sudo_spawn_watchdog` in `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` spawned the keepalive
watchdog via:

\```bash
setsid bash -c '…' _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
local pid=$!
\```

The goal was "new session, detached from the controlling TTY, survives the
invoking run-script's exit." On Linux `setsid(1)` does that. On macOS there
is no `setsid(1)` in base — Apple ships `setsid(2)` as a libc system call
(accessible from C, Python's `start_new_session=True`, etc.) but no CLI
wrapper. Homebrew has a keg-only `util-linux` formula which would provide
it, but this repo doesn't force-link it and most Macs don't have it.

When `setsid` isn't on `$PATH`, the backgrounded invocation does this:

1. Shell forks a child to run `setsid bash -c '…' &`
2. The child tries to `execvp("setsid", …)`, fails with `ENOENT`
3. Child prints `setsid: command not found` → redirected to `/dev/null` →
   invisible
4. Child exits with status 127 → zombie reaped by shell
5. Parent sets `pid=$!` to that dead child's PID (correct PID, dead process)
6. Parent writes that PID into `keepalive.pid`

On the next run-script, `_sudo_state_valid` checks:

\```bash
kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1   # ← fails here: PID is dead
\```

Returns non-zero → `sudo_session_init` thinks the state is stale → line 236
`rm -rf "$dir"` wipes the still-valid password files → re-prompt.

The `sudo -S -v -p ''` validation a few lines later (line 110) would have
worked — `sudo.pass` is fine — but the `kill -0` check runs first and
short-circuits.

## Workaround

Fixed in-tree. The fix in `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` is to detect `setsid`
at runtime and fall back to `nohup` on systems without it:

\```bash
if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    setsid bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
else
    nohup bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
fi
\```

Plus `trap "" HUP` at the top of the child body so SIGHUP on controlling-TTY
hangup is ignored even in the `nohup` branch (belt-and-suspenders — `nohup`
already does this, but making it explicit in the body means the behaviour
is identical between the two branches).

`nohup` is in base macOS (`/usr/bin/nohup`) and in util-linux on Linux, so
this fallback is universally available. It doesn't create a new session
like `setsid` does, but for the actual requirement here ("survive the
parent run-script's exit") the `&` + `disown` + stdin/stdout/stderr-to-
`/dev/null` + SIGHUP-ignored combination is sufficient.

Verification on a fresh `chezmoi apply` after the fix:

\```bash
$ grep -c 'sudo password' <apply-log>    # should be 1, not 3
1

$ PID=$(cat "$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)/keepalive.pid")
$ kill -0 "$PID" && echo alive
alive
\```

If you're debugging a machine that already has the stale state dir, wipe it
manually before the next apply:

\```bash
rm -rf "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)"    # or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR on Linux
\```

## Prevention

- Any new "detach a long-lived helper from this shell" in this repo must
  either use the pattern above (setsid-with-nohup-fallback) or go through
  a launchd agent. Don't add raw `setsid` calls to new shell scripts.
- When reviewing future edits to `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`, check the
  watchdog spawn on macOS too — Linux CI passes silently for this class of
  bug because `setsid` always works there. The CLAUDE.md invariant "Sudo
  session is shared across all run-scripts" covers the `sudo -k` footgun
  but not the silent-watchdog-death footgun; this pitfall is the record.
- Long-term option: install util-linux via Homebrew in the ansible
  `devtools` role on macOS, symlink `setsid` into `~/.local/bin`. Not
  worth the keg-only linking complexity right now; the `nohup` fallback is
  simpler and less invasive.

## Related

- [CLAUDE.md → Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts](../CLAUDE.md) —
  the invariant this pitfall is a failure mode of
- [`docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md`](../docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md) —
  helper API, state dir layout, cleanup model
- [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) —
  `_sudo_spawn_watchdog` is where the fix lives
- Apple's `setsid(2)` man page confirms the syscall exists but a CLI
  wrapper is not shipped — this is Apple's choice, not an oversight, so
  the workaround needs to live in this repo indefinitely

157	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
158	
159	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`. The user is prompted **once** at the start of `chezmoi apply` and downstream scripts reuse the cached credential silently.
160	
161	**Hard rules** when touching run-scripts:
162	
163	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
164	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the shared cache for the whole flow).
165	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
166	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always pipe via `sudo -S <file`.
167	
168	Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script:
169	
170	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
171	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag (mirror existing run-scripts).
172	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
173	4. Run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (simple cases) or pass `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` to ansible.
174	
175	Full helper API, runtime state, cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
176	
177	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet_apply.py` over
178	SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file
179	path) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. The helper validates with `sudo -S
180	-v -p ''` and writes into the same shared state dir, so downstream
181	run-scripts see the cached state and never re-prompt. Do **not** read
182	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from your run-script directly — always go
183	through `sudo_session_init`. See [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md)
184	→ "Non-interactive password injection" and [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md)
185	for the orchestrator side.
186	
187	### fleet-apply semantics (counter-intuitive defaults)
188	
189	A few `just fleet-apply*` behaviours WILL trip up agents who don't know them. Full docs in [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md); the load-bearing invariants:
190	
191	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host is shown as yellow ⚠ `drift` in the live table and the per-file paths are listed, but it does **not** count toward the exit code. Don't "fix" drift hosts unless the user asks. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.

114	_sudo_spawn_watchdog() {
115	    local state_dir="$1"
116	    local watch_pid="$2"
117	    # Goal: detach the watchdog from the current shell's TTY + session so it
118	    # survives a run-script exit and keeps the shared state dir alive across
119	    # subsequent run-scripts in the same chezmoi apply.
120	    #
121	    # `setsid(1)` is the clean way (new session, no controlling TTY) but it
122	    # only ships by default on Linux (util-linux). macOS has setsid(2) as a
123	    # libc call but no setsid(1) in base — see pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md.
124	    # Using `setsid` unconditionally caused every run-script to re-prompt for
125	    # sudo on macOS because $! captured a short-lived "command not found"
126	    # shell, and _sudo_state_valid's `kill -0` probe then invalidated the dir.
127	    #
128	    # Fallback: `nohup` (present on macOS and Linux) + `trap "" HUP` in the
129	    # child + `disown` in the parent. Not a new session, but the watchdog
130	    # survives parent shell exit, which is what we actually need here.
131	    # SC2016: body is passed to the child `bash -c` where $1/$2 are its own
132	    # positional params, so single-quoting is intentional (no expansion here).
133	    # shellcheck disable=SC2016
134	    local body='
135	        trap "" HUP
136	        STATE_DIR="$1"
137	        WATCH_PID="$2"
138	        # WHY: the real "keep-alive" is the sudo.pass + `sudo -S` pattern —
139	        # we still refresh the timestamp opportunistically so short-lived
140	        # downstream callers may benefit. Failures (tty_tickets mismatch,
141	        # stale password) are swallowed; they are not cleanup triggers.
142	        while kill -0 "$WATCH_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
143	            sudo -S -v -p "" <"$STATE_DIR/sudo.pass" 2>/dev/null || true
144	            sleep 50
145	        done
146	        rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
147	    '
148	    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
149	        setsid bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
150	    else
151	        nohup bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
152	    fi
153	    local pid=$!

sudo-shared: nohup fallback for macOS (setsid(1) not in base → 3x re-prompt)

_sudo_spawn_watchdog used `setsid bash -c '…' &` unconditionally. macOS
ships setsid(2) as a libc call but no setsid(1) CLI, so the backgrounded
command failed with "command not found" silently (stderr → /dev/null),
$! captured the already-exited shell PID, and _sudo_state_valid's
kill -0 probe then wiped the state dir on every subsequent run-script —
producing three separate sudo prompts in one `chezmoi apply` despite
the "entered once, reused" wording.

Fix: detect `setsid` at runtime, fall back to `nohup` (present on both
macOS and Linux) with `trap "" HUP` in the child body. Not a new
session, but survives parent-script exit, which is the actual
requirement. Linux hosts keep the `setsid` path unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"
